units.label: Title: Color Theory: The Color Wheel
Definition: primary, secondary, tertiary (text)
units.content_summary: Primary colors (red, yellow, blue) cannot be made by mixing others. Secondary colors (orange, green, purple) are made by mixing two primaries. Tertiary colors are made by mixing a primary with an adjacent secondary.

units.label: Color wheel diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Full 12-section color wheel showing primary colors evenly spaced, secondary colors between them, and tertiary colors filling the remaining gaps, arranged in a circle.

units.label: Complementary colors (text)
units.content_summary: Complementary colors sit directly opposite each other on the wheel (e.g. red-green, blue-orange). When placed side by side, they create strong visual contrast and make each other appear more vivid.

units.label: Complementary pairs example (image)
units.content_summary: Color wheel with three complementary pairs connected by lines through the center: red-green, blue-orange, yellow-purple, each pair shown as adjacent swatches for comparison.

units.label: Practice: identify color relationships (text)
units.content_summary: Four questions using a blank color wheel: identify a given color's complement; name two secondary colors adjacent to a given primary; classify a listed color as primary, secondary, or tertiary.
